subject: Re: Narrowing IP indemnity carve-out & escrow option

Subject: IP indemnity carve-out — suggested narrowing

Marcus,

Thanks for sending the MSA redlines this morning. Our GC ran the IP indemnity section by the product team and they flagged the size of the liability cap carve-out tied to IP infringement. To move forward quickly we want to propose two adjustments:

- Narrow the carve-out to proven third-party claims for actual monetary damages caused by infringement (i.e., no broader consequences or punitive-type remedies).
- Place an express cap on the indemnity payout tied to the claim (we're suggesting a 2x the annual order value for the offending product rather than an open-ended exposure).

We're also open to an escrow mechanism for funds while the parties litigate the claim — that helps our procurement team with budgeting and reduces the need for a large up-front holdback. Attached is our redline (Forte - Redlines v2.docx) with inline comments.

Can Redwood provide sample language that preserves your core IP indemnity promise but limits the carrier-like open exposure? Happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

Best,
Sarah Klein
Senior Counsel, Forte Health

Sarah — thanks for the quick review and the redlines. Appreciate the practical approach.

Two quick clarifications from our side before Laura and legal get into markup:
1) By "2x the annual order value" do you mean 2x the then-current 12-month committed spend under the order form, or 2x expected annualized spend for the impacted product line? That changes the tail risk calculation for us.
2) On escrow: are you proposing a third-party escrow (we have preferred escrow language) or an internal holdback managed by Forte pending resolution?

Laura — looping you in to propose language that: (a) maintains Redwood's indemnity for third-party IP claims for actual damages, (b) limits consequential/double-recovery exposure, and (c) offers an escrow approach as an alternative to an uncapped carve-out. Subject: Proposed MSA language for IP indemnity carve-out

Marcus / Sarah — drafting note below; this is intended as a middle-ground that protects Redwood from open-ended exposure while preserving customer remedies for third-party infringement. Please consider as a tracked-change replacement for the current §8.2 language.

Proposed replacement (redline text suggestion):
"Seller (Redwood) shall defend and indemnify Buyer (Customer) against any final judgment arising from a third-party claim that the delivery of the licensed Services, as delivered by Seller and used in accordance with the Agreement, infringes any United States or European patents, copyrights, or trade secrets. Seller's indemnity obligation for such claims shall be limited to the actual monetary damages awarded to Buyer, plus reasonable attorneys' fees and court costs, provided that Seller's aggregate indemnity payments under this Section shall not exceed two times (2x) the Customer's annual recurring spend under the relevant Order Form in effect at the time the claim is first submitted to Seller."

Escrow option (alternate):
"Instead of direct payment, upon initiation of a covered third-party claim Seller may, at its election, arrange for a third-party escrow to hold an amount equal to Seller's estimated exposure (not to exceed 2x ARR) pending final resolution, provided that escrowed funds shall only be released pursuant to a final judgment or mutually agreed settlement resolving the claim."

Two operational notes: (1) we would want a mechanism to dispute the initial escrow estimate (independent accountant or arbitrator) and (2) carve-out should not extend to injunctive or equitable remedies — those remain available to Buyer without monetary payment from Seller.

Sarah — does this track with Forte's risk appetite? If you want, we can create a tracked-change doc and a redline that inserts the 2x language into the MSA.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura — this is helpful and closer to what our GC was willing to accept. A few follow-ups from our side after reviewing your suggested language:

- The 2x ARR cap is acceptable in principle but we need the baseline to be clearly defined: please specify "Customer's annual recurring spend under the relevant Order Form during the 12 months immediately preceding the date the claim is first submitted to Seller."
- We want the escrow alternative to include a neutral third-party administrator and an explicit dispute path (binding expert determination) if either party contests the initial escrow amount.
- On equitable remedies: Forte needs confirmation that injunctive relief seeking a halt to alleged infringement is not restricted by the indemnity/cap language. Your text suggests injunctive remedies "remain available" but please add an explicit sentence to that effect.

I've attached a short PDF (Proposed_IP_Escrow_Terms.pdf) with our model escrow admin language. If you can produce a final tracked-change MSA by Thursday EOD, Procurement will route for a commercial sign-off next week.

Thanks,
Sarah
